title: Compassion
note: He defines compassion as mercy that goes out naturally to all living beings, with no tie behind it. It matters to renunciation as loving-kindness does to household life, so it comes first.

couplets.plain: The wealth of compassion is the wealth among wealth. Wealth in goods is found even among the low.
couplets.pm: The finest of all wealth is the wealth that comes from compassion: tending living beings and rising by that righteousness. It is found only in the high, and it is the wealth of distinction. The wealth of goods is found even in the low and has no distinction.

links.quote: The wealth of compassion is the wealth among wealth
links.reason: Compassion is valued above goods, which even the low can have.
Compassion takes the title of chief wealth from anything merely material.

couplets.plain: Search by good ways and hold to compassion. Test it by many ways, and it is still your only support.
couplets.pm: Stand on the good path of perception, inference, scripture and reason, ask what righteousness will support you, and be compassionate. Examine it by every creed, though they clash with one another, and compassion is still the only support. It never leaves the soul and helps in both worlds.

links.quote: it is still your only support
links.reason: However many ways you test it, compassion remains the one support.

couplets.plain: Those whose hearts are full of compassion don’t enter the dark, painful world.
couplets.pm: Those whose hearts are dense with compassion don’t enter the world of pain dense with darkness. That is a hell of thick darkness that torments all who enter it. It is called a world because it is a place in the worlds below.

links.reason: A heart full of compassion is spared the world of pain.

couplets.plain: They say that those who tend living beings and hold to compassion have no deeds that make their own soul afraid.
couplets.pm: The knowing say that someone who tends living beings and is compassionate towards them has no evil deeds to make their own soul afraid. Souls are eternal, so they are called enduring. Such a person doesn’t kill or commit such sins, and so doesn’t enter hell.

links.quote: tend living beings and hold to compassion
links.reason: Tending living beings shields a person from deeds their own soul fears.

couplets.plain: Those who hold to compassion have no misery. The great rich earth, where the wind moves, is witness.
couplets.pm: The compassionate have no suffering even in this life. All who live on the great rich earth where the wind moves are witness. No one, at any time or place, has seen the compassionate suffer, so by that absence all are witnesses.

links.quote: Those who hold to compassion have no misery
links.reason: Calls the whole earth as witness that misery does not touch the compassionate.

couplets.plain: They say that those who leave compassion and go on doing wrong have left what truly matters and forgotten.
couplets.pm: The good say that those who give up compassion towards living beings and go on doing cruel things did no righteousness before, and have forgotten the suffering they now endure, the three kinds that come with birth. If they remembered, they wouldn’t live like this.
couplets.note: பொருள் usually means wealth. Here he takes it as righteousness, the thing of true worth.

links.quote: leave compassion and go on doing wrong
links.reason: Abandoning compassion to do wrong is called forgetting what truly matters.

couplets.plain: That world is not for those without compassion, as this world is not for those without wealth.
couplets.pm: Those without compassion towards living beings have no joy of the world of liberation, just as those without wealth have no joy of this world. Wealth is the cause of this world’s pleasures, and compassion of that world’s.
couplets.sensitive: says this world is not for the poor

links.quote: That world is not for those without compassion
links.reason: Without compassion the next world is shut, as this one is to those without wealth.

couplets.plain: Those who lose wealth may flower again one day. Those who lose compassion are lost, and will hardly rise.
couplets.pm: Those made poor by fate may leave poverty behind and flourish with wealth at a later time. Those without compassion, whose sin never ends, are ruined for good and never rise again. The last couplet likened the two, and this one says that this loss is worse.

links.quote: Those who lose compassion are lost
links.reason: A lack of wealth can be made good, but a lack of compassion hardly ever can.

links.quote: Those who lose wealth may flower again one day. Those who lose compassion are lost
links.reason: Sets the loss of compassion against the loss of wealth and finds only the first incurable.

couplets.plain: Look closely at the righteousness done by someone without compassion. It is like a confused person glimpsing the truth.
couplets.pm: The righteousness done by someone with no compassion for living beings is like a person without wisdom grasping the truth for a moment. Lack of wisdom soon destroys that truth, and lack of compassion destroys the righteousness the same way. So compassion is the root of all other righteousness.

links.quote: the righteousness done by someone without compassion
links.reason: Righteousness without compassion is no surer than a confused mind glimpsing the truth.

couplets.plain: When you go against those weaker than you, think of yourself before those stronger.
couplets.pm: When someone without compassion goes to harm the weak, let them think of how they stand in fear before the strong who come to harm them. “Weaker” includes animals as well as people. Thinking of this, they learn that this creature has the same fear, and compassion for it arises. This is how compassion is born.

links.quote: go against those weaker than you
think of yourself before those stronger

ideaLinks.quote: have no deeds that make their own soul afraid
ideaLinks.reason: Deeds the soul fears do not belong to one who tends living beings with compassion.
